description:
You are a medical scientist analyzing cancer cell migration. You have a time-lapse microscopy dataset of HeLa cells (nuclei labeled with H2B-GFP) loaded in Fiji.

Your goal is to measure the migration velocity of these cells using kymograph analysis.

1. Identify moving nuclei in the time-lapse stack.
2. Draw a straight line (at least 200 pixels long) along the path of migration of several cells.
3. Generate a kymograph (Space-Time plot) using 'Image > Stacks > Reslice [/]...' or 'Analyze > Multi Kymograph > Multi Kymograph'.
4. In the resulting kymograph image, measuring the slope of the streaks corresponds to velocity. Identify at least 3 distinct cell tracks (diagonal streaks).
5. Measure the velocity for these tracks. You can measure the angle or dimensions (dx, dy) manually.
   - Calibration: Pixel size = 0.645 µm, Time interval = 30 min (0.5 hr).
   - Formula: Velocity (µm/hr) = (dx_pixels * 0.645) / (dy_frames * 0.5)

6. Save your outputs to ~/Fiji_Data/results/kymograph/:
   - 'kymograph_main.png': The generated kymograph image.
   - 'velocity_measurements.csv': A CSV file with columns 'track_id', 'velocity_um_per_hr' (and optionally dx, dt, angle). Must contain at least 3 measurements.
   - 'kymograph_report.txt': A text summary containing the number of tracks measured and the mean velocity.

Anti-gaming: Ensure all files are created during this session. Do not use fake data.
